content.text: Zero defects flagged. Final visual confirmation of all three:

All three sizes are done and verified. **Output:** `portrait.png` (1080×1350), `wide.png` (1200×1000), `sky.png` (300×600) — exact pixel dimensions confirmed. **How it's built:** one `template.html` with a single scale knob (`html { font-size: SCALE * 16px }`, every dimension in `rem`), compiled to three HTML files at 1×, 0.85×, and 0.28×. Typography, icons, gaps, and padding all scale together; the layout itself is a full-height flex column so bands stretch to the real viewport width at each size. **Key decisions to make all three work:** - **Photo band** is the flexible element (`flex: 3 1 auto`, min-height, `max-height: 42vh`), so it absorbs leftover height in the tall sky format and gives up height in the short wide format. `object-fit: cover` means it always crops, never distorts — the `` box measured 1080×514, 1200×289, and 300×252, each filled by a cover crop. - **Focal point** set to `50% 72%`. My first pass used 42%, which in the wide format sliced exactly along the horizon and left an almost-empty sky band with a stray green sliver; 72% keeps both hills and the red marker in frame at every aspect. - **Even columns** via `flex: 1 1 0` with `min-width: 0` — measured left edges 36/380/724 (portrait), 31/417/803 (wide), 10/106/201 (sky), equal widths throughout. **Verification:** I wrote an audit script that loads each page at its true viewport and checks document scroll size vs. viewport (overflow), element bounds vs. canvas edges (cut-off text), scroll vs. client box (clipping), and sibling section rectangles (overlap). Final run reported `bad: []` for all three, with `scrollWidth/Height` exactly equal to each viewport. Two defects were found and fixed along the way: the horizon crop, and the CTA headline's `line-height: 1` leaving zero slack around the cap box (now 1.16).
